title: The sharp Fischer-type determinantal inequality for accretive-dissipative matrices
statement:
Let $A\in \mathbb{M}_{n}(\bold C)$ be an accretive-dissipative matrix, partitioned as

$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}A_{11}&A_{12}\\A_{21}&A_{22}\end{pmatrix},
$$

where $A_{11}$ is an $m\times m$ principal block and $A_{22}$ is the complementary block. **Sharp Fischer-type determinantal inequality.** One should have

$$
|\det A|\leq 2^m|\det A_{11}|\,|\det A_{22}|.
$$

The preceding argument proves the same inequality with the larger factor $2^{3m/2}$, so this conjecture asks whether the constant can be reduced to $2^m$.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.4949

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2012).
source_name: Minghua Lin, “Fischer type determinantal inequalities for accretive-dissipative matrices”, arXiv:1209.4949 (2012).
